question.text: If the INR interest rate rises from 7% to 8% while USD rate stays at 5%, what happens to the USDINR 1-year futures price (spot = 83)?

answer.text: It increases from approximately 84.58 to approximately 85.37
It decreases because higher INR rates attract FPI flows
It remains unchanged because spot hasn't moved
It becomes exactly equal to the spot rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the IRP formula (pp. 62-63), the old one-year USDINR futures price at 7% INR and 5% USD is approximately 84.58. With INR raised to 8%, F = 83 x 1.08 / 1.05 = 85.37. Everything else held constant, the wider interest-rate differential widens the forward premium (pp. 122, 125). The Trap: Higher INR rates INCREASE the futures price by widening the forward premium, even though they may have other effects in the spot market. Note: The question isolates the IRP effect: only the INR rate changes, and everything else is held constant.
